question: What percentage of respiratory specimens tested for influenza in U.S. clinical laboratories will be positive in CDC's FluView report for Week 44 (week ending November 7, 2026)?

calls.reasoning: Week 42 printed 7.6% (up from 5.7, 5.0, 3.9); weekly growth ratios ~1.14-1.33, avg ~1.25. Two weeks of compounding at that rate gives ~11.9%. Reference class: 2022-23 early H3N2 wave went 5.47 (wk42) -> 12.75 (wk44), ~1.5x/week. Upward: H1N1 G155E antigenic drift, West Coast positivity ~19%, hospital admissions +27% w/w, 8/10 regions rising. Downward: some regions flat, wk40->41 slowdown, specimen-mix noise, initial-edition values can run below revised. No human prediction market found (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold searched). Median ~11.6.
sources: WebSearch: flu positivity November 2026 H1N1 surge (Dr. Ruth Report 11/1/26 snippet: SF flu A positivity 19.2%)
WebSearch: Becker's/medicaldaily FluView week 42 notes (admissions 6,100, +27% w/w)
WebSearch: Kalshi/Polymarket flu percent positive (none found)

- 2026 series of clinical lab % positive: Wk37 2.7, Wk39 3.9, Wk40 5.0, Wk41 5.7, Wk42 7.6. Weekly ratios: 1.28 (39->40), 1.14 (40->41), 1.33 (41->42).

- Wk42 ILI 2.4%, up but below 2.9% baseline; NHSN admissions 6,100 (+27% from 4,811); FluSurv-NET 1.3/100k weekly; Wk41 hosp rate highest for that week since 2010-11.
- Press (Nov 1 2026 Substack snippet): San Francisco flu A test positivity 19.2%; West Coast early surge tied to H1N1 with HA G155E mutation (possible partial immune escape).
- 2022-23 reference (CDC archive, revised figures, clinical labs): Wk40 2.76, Wk41 3.57, Wk42 5.47, Wk43 8.52, Wk44 12.75 (Wk42->Wk44 ratio 2.33, ~1.53/week).
- Other recent seasons were in mid-single digits by early-mid November (per question background).
- Status quo/naive persistence: Wk44 = 7.6 (latest printed); simple continuation of avg recent growth (~1.25/wk) gives ~11.9.
- Week 43 edition (week ending Oct 31) not yet published as of Nov 2; due Nov 6.
- Resolves off the Week 44 FluView edition's clinical-lab table 'No. of positive specimens (%)' for Week 44 as first printed (published ~Nov 13), not later revisions.
- Event window: MMWR week 44 = Nov 1-7, 2026; as of Nov 2 12:40 UTC ~25% elapsed; publication Nov 13.
- No Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold market found on this metric.
- Searched but not found: Week 43 FluView numbers, national wastewater flu A level for late Oct, ED flu visit percentages.
calls.reference_class: Early-season fast-rising US influenza waves (2022-23, current 2026-27 weeks 39-42): 2-week multiplicative change in NREVSS clinical lab % positive during exponential growth phase

Weekly multiplicative growth 1.1-1.33x over W39-W42; two more weeks to W44 gives ~9-12.8%, with linear +1.9pt/wk giving ~11.4%. - Series (CDC FluView, initial editions): W37 2.7%, W39 3.9%, W40 5.0%, W41 5.7%, W42 7.6%. Week-on-week multiplicative growth ~1.10-1.33x; last step +1.9 pts.

- Strain: H1N1 with HA G155E mutation, first seen in Seattle in Sept; possible partial immune escape/vaccine mismatch (Today.com, CNN, Northeastern, Oct 22 2026).

- Status quo: continued rise; week-to-week fall changes typically flat to +2 pts; local plateaus/dips occur; early-leading regions (West, R10) may level off first.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the initial Week 44 FluView edition's clinical-lab 'No. of positive specimens (%)' cell (national), not later revisions or public-health-lab data.

calls.reference_class: Early-November week-over-week trajectory of NREVSS clinical-lab flu percent positive in early-onset seasons (2022-23, 2009) and the current 2026-27 growth series W37-W42

calls.reasoning: Week 42 printed 7.6% (up from 5.7, 5.0, 3.9), H1N1-driven with the G155E mutation. Hospital admissions were up 27% week on week and positivity rose in 8 of 10 HHS regions. Weekly growth ratios of 1.14-1.33 project 10-13.4% two weeks out. 2022-23 analog: 5.5% to 12.75% from Week 42 to 44. calls.reconciliation: The wastewater dispute (CDC Very Low/Low for the week ending Oct 17 vs WastewaterSCAN High nationally on Oct 23) cannot be settled without web access. They are different networks on different dates, so both may hold; given little weight. The 2022-23 analog figures from Run 1 (fetched) are consistent with Run 3's recollection; accepted. All runs agree there is no market and no Week 43 data. The remaining difference is judgment on growth: I take ~1.20x a week, below the recent ~1.25 average, because Regions 1 and 10 were plateauing. Median 11.0, with dispersion similar to Runs 2 and 3 but slightly wider.
